text:
Nadia: Quick sync post-RFC: I want to propose a 'traffic contraction lane' concept instead of just 'fallback'. The idea: controller issues 'contraction verdicts' with a suggested contraction plan and a safety token. Router applies progressively.

Ibrahim: Love the token idea. helps with idempotency and audit. What fields are in a verdict token?

Clara: Minimal: verdict_id, action (contract/hold), confidence, signature, suggested_steps. Signed by controller for Private installs.

Maks: Also include budget_consumed and safety_budget_left so routers can decide if they should escalate to full fallback or a gentle throttling.

Nadia: Good call. We should standardize metric normalization. Propose these signals: latency_p95_norm (0..1), downstream_err_rate (0..1), semantic_quality_drop (0..1). Blend using "confidence_blend" weights that are configurable per-tenant.

Ibrahim: On windowing: prefer two-window scheme — a short reactive window (20s) for rapid signals and a longer stability window (5m) for confirmation. Only emit contraction if short window triggers AND long window > threshold_x. avoids flip-flopping.

Clara: Router-side hysteresis: multiply controller confidence by a local multiplier based on recent flips. e.g., local_conf = controller_conf * (1 - flip_decay). That keeps routers conservative after recent rollbacks.

Maks: How do we test verdicts? Suggest a 'verdict-replay' harness in staging that replays sampled traffic and compares router behavior against a golden simulator. Fail if simulated success rate drops >1% after contraction.

Nadia: API sketch: POST /v1/verdicts { tenant, metrics, sample_id } -> 200 { token, verdict_id, action, confidence, signature, suggested_steps }

Ibrahim: Example payload returned by controller (single-line to keep small):
```json
{"token":"v=1;id=vd-2026-abc;sig=...","action":"contract","confidence":"0.81","suggested_steps":"[{\"from\":100,\"to\":40,\"step\":15,\"window_s\":45}]"}
```

Clara: Router execution rules: accept signed token OR fall back to policy-cache. If token indicates contract, apply suggested_steps but enforce min_step_time and max_step to prevent oscillation.

Maks: For Private deployments with no controller reachability, local agent should generate provisional tokens with `provisional:true` and record full provenance; controller will reconcile later. provisional tokens have lower local_conf cap.

Nadia: Security/compliance: tokens must be signed using KMS keys (hosted) or HSM-signed for on-prem. Audit log must include raw metrics snapshot and decision hash.

Ibrahim: Operational metrics to emit: verdict_rate, avg_confidence, token_verification_latency, router_apply_success, revert_count. Dashboards + SLOs needed.

Clara: We should add a "safety budget" per tenant. Each contraction consumes budget proportional to scope and time. If budget exhausted, escalate to manual review. This prevents autopilot from repeatedly throttling the same tenant.

Maks: Rollout plan: POC with one low-risk service, staged enablement: 1) controller emits tokens only, 2) router honors tokens in passive mode (metrics only), 3) active enforcement for small % traffic, 4) full enforcement.

Nadia: Edge-case: what if controller is compromised? Make sure routers enforce maximum change caps and always require signature. Also include a revocation list endpoint: GET /v1/verdicts/revoked -> list of verdict_ids. Routers should check revocations periodically.

Ibrahim: Testing: add unit tests for token parsing/verif, e2e tests with staging canary, and chaos test where controller disappears mid-contraction.

Clara: UX: build a tiny curator UI where SRE/product can preview a suggested contraction with timeline and safety budget impact before enabling auto-apply.

Maks: Dev note: keep adjudicate latency <60ms median. Use GRPC+protobuf for hosted controller -> faster than JSON over HTTP for high qps. Controller->router token exchange can be compact.

Nadia: Action items: Ibrahim -> proto + token format draft (RDW-11021) by Thu; Clara -> dashboard metrics + safety budget model (SRE-2200); Maks -> staging POC plan + test harness (ENG-3344); Nadia -> write follow-up RFC with API samples and revocation semantics.

Ibrahim: I'll also prototype a small verifier library for router side (rust + go).

Clara: :thumbsup:

Maks: :+1: deploy note?

DeployBot: canary-verdict-service v0.0.3 promoted to staging.

Nadia: Nice. We'll pair on the RFC next week and include the replay harness design.
